channel.title: Megajournal Feed
channel.description: Aggregated research articles from the multidisciplinary megajournals: Nature Communications, restricted to biological and health sciences, and Science Advances, which is not filtered by subject because no accessible source exposes one.

item.title: Nature Communications: A family of small proteins links c-di-GMP riboswitch signaling with sporulation in Clostridioides difficile
item.description: The second messenger c-di-GMP inhibits sporulation in the pathogenic bacterium Clostridioides difficile through unclear mechanisms. Here, Badilla Lobo et al. show that the expression of sporulation genes is modulated by a family of small membrane-associated proteins encoded by genes that are controlled by c-diGMP-regulated riboswitches.

item.title: Nature Communications: Multivalent antiviral conjugates enhance activity against Influenza via cross-linking viruses
item.description: A multivalent antiviral conjugates (AVCs) platform was established by conjugating NA inhibitors and Fc domain. AVCs cross-link flu viruses, blocking entry and release. Trivalent peramivir-Fc conjugate outperformed clinical drugs in mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: A CCL21 gene-modified dendritic cell vaccine combined with pembrolizumab in advanced non-small cell lung cancer: a phase I trial
item.description: Feasibility and safety profile of intratumoral administration of a DC vaccine overexpressing CCL21 (CCL21-DC) have been previously reported in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Here the authors report safety, clinical outcomes and immunological correlates of a phase I trial of CCL21-DC in combination with anti-PD1 pembrolizumab in patients with advanced NSCLC.

item.title: Nature Communications: Herbicide degradation is driven by communication-mediated division of labor in synthetic communities
item.description: Herbicide residues threaten soil health. Researchers constructed two SynComs that degrade multiple herbicides via quorum sensing-mediated metabolic division of labor, and maize pot trials verify their bioremediation efficacy.

item.title: Nature Communications: Near-atomistic simulations reveal the molecular principles that control chromatin structure and phase separation
item.description: Russell et al. introduce a 10 × faster, chemically detailed chromatin model bridging molecular and genomic scales, revealing how DNA sequence, spacing and histone acetylation govern chromatin folding and phase separation.

item.title: Nature Communications: The structural dynamics and molecular coupling in the slow inactivation of a prokaryotic voltage-gated sodium channel
item.description: Slow inactivation of voltage-gated sodium channels is important for regulating cellular excitability. Here the authors probe the conformational dynamics in the selectivity filter using smFRET and reveal the critical residue pair that mediates conformational communication between the primary and slow inactivation gates

item.title: Nature Communications: Top-down semantic predictions align phonetic neuronal dynamics in human superior temporal gyrus
item.description: How semantic information influences phonetic processing during speech perception remains unclear. Here, the authors show that semantic predictions reshape phonetic representations in human temporal cortex at the level of neuronal population activity.

item.title: Nature Communications: DCAF7 regulates hematopoietic stem cell function and differentiation through polycomb repressive complex 1 modulation
item.description: This study identifies DCAF7 as a new regulator of blood stem cells showing how it controls chromatin to preserve stem cell function with implications for understanding normal and malignant blood formation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Saturation mutagenesis enables RAD51D clinical variant interpretation and identifies distinct biochemical functions
item.description: RAD51D is a tumor suppressor gene where pathogenic variants are associated with increased risk of breast and ovarian cancer. This study reports a high throughput functional screen of 6,888 RAD51D coding variants along with analysis of 70 clinically-identified breast and ovarian cancer variants.

Nature Communications: Spatial transcriptomics reveals microenvironmental heterogeneity in osteoarthritic subchondral bone
item.description: Subchondral bone remodeling is increasingly implicated in osteoarthritis, but its spatial organization remain incompletely understood. This study provides a high-resolution spatial map of subchondral bone and identifies conserved spatial architectures, revealing distinct microenvironmental states and candidate signaling pathways associated with subchondral bone sclerosis.

item.title: Nature Communications: A model of brain function to predict tau across Alzheimer’s disease and related disorders
item.description: Researchers developed a machine learning model using FDG-PET imaging to accurately predict Alzheimer’s-type tau pathology across spectrums of aging and dementia, providing a novel framework to estimate tau burden non-invasively.

item.title: Nature Communications: First-line dolutegravir/lamivudine in HIV-1 infection: lymph node penetration and reservoir decline in a randomized open-label clinical trial
item.description: In this study, Jose Molto and colleagues report data from a randomised open-label clinical trial showing of first-line dolutegravir/lamivudine treatment for HIV-1. They report that the treatment reaches lymph nodes and regions containing HIV-positive cells, which strengthens evidence for antiviral exposure within a key anatomical HIV reservoir.

item.title: Nature Communications: Characterization of chemoresistant cell populations improves risk stratification and therapy prediction in pediatric acute myeloid leukemia
item.description: Early risk prediction is essential to decide the treatment procedure for pediatric acute myeloid leukemia. Here, the authors show that rare chemoresistant cell populations, detectable at diagnosis, improve risk stratification and reveal potential targets for more effective, personalized therapies.

item.title: Nature Communications: Immune correlates of protection are exposure-dependent: evidence from the Dominican Republic
item.description: This study shows that antibody levels linked to protection against SARS-CoV-2 infection vary with transmission intensity, suggesting immune correlates of protection depend on exposure context.

item.title: Nature Communications: Cannabinoid modulation of central amygdala population dynamics during threat investigation
item.description: Neural mechanisms underlying cannabinoids’ anxiogenic effects are not fully understood. Here authors show that cannabinoids dose-dependently increased spontaneous activity of central amygdala (CeA) neurons expressing somatostatin (SOM), altered CeA activity patterns during threat processing, and enhanced defensive behavior. Ex vivo studies in brain slices further showed that cannabinoids reduce inhibitory input from neighboring neurons, releasing a “brake” on SOM activity.

item.title: Nature Communications: Synthetic lethal screens reveal p300/CBP as a vulnerability for GNAQ -driven uveal melanomas
item.description: Uveal melanoma (UM) is often driven by mutations in GNAQ. Here, authors identify p300 as a synthetic lethal target in GNAQ-mutant UM and show that p300 inhibition impairs tumour growth and metastasis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Tonicity drives collecting duct maturation in the mammalian kidney
item.description: Organ maturation is an emerging focus in the fields of organoid and developmental biology. The authors show that high tonicity drives the maturation of renal collecting ducts in vitro and in vivo, improving morphology, gene expression, and function.

item.title: Nature Communications: Different concentrations of atropine in children with high myopia: a 2-year multicenter double-blind, randomized controlled trial
item.description: Here the authors report the results of a multicenter, double-blind, randomized-controlled trial that evaluates the effect and safety of different concentration atropine eyedrops (0.01%, 0.04%, 0.10%) for myopia control in children with high myopia. The findings show that nightly use of 0.10% atropine eye drops for 24 months mitigated myopia progression with an acceptable safety profile.

item.title: Nature Communications: Genome mining of the tumor microbiome reveals biosynthetic diversity and potential pathology-modulating metabolites
item.description: Here, Pulliam and colleagues characterize the metabolites encoded by tumor-inhabiting microbes and their potential role in cancer pathology.

item.title: Nature Communications: Structural basis of voltage gating in a partially activated K + channel
item.description: The process by which the voltage sensor electromechanically couples to the pore in K+ channels is not fully understood. A cryo-EM structure of a partially activated state, together with computational modeling and MD simulations, clarifies the mechanistic basis for electromechanical coupling.

item.title: Nature Communications: Untargeted screening of drug-like compounds using high-throughput metabolomics uncovers inhibitors of key biological pathways
item.description: Metabolomics is widely used in drug development to reveal mechanisms of action. Here, the authors identify drug-like compounds with potent enzyme engagement by screening 1,020 compounds of unknown function, allowing them to discover nucleotide synthesis inhibitors and an atrophy reversing glutathione activator.

item.title: Nature Communications: Evaluating generative models for structure-based drug discovery from de novo design to lead optimization
item.description: Protein structures are increasingly available but turning them into useful drug candidates remains difficult. Here, Cao et al. introduce MolGenBench to assess 17 generative methods and reveal gaps in activity, target awareness and generalization.

item.title: Nature Communications: Substrate coupling and inhibition in human Na + -dependent Cl − /HCO 3 − exchanger NCBE (SLC4A10)
item.description: NCBE (SLC4A10) is important for cerebrospinal fluid pH regulation. Here, authors determine cryo-EM structures of human NCBE that reveal ion binding, inhibitor recognition, and the structural basis of substrate coupling in this transporter.

item.title: Nature Communications: Phosphorylation tunes electrostatically driven protein-RNA interactions
item.description: Phosphorylation can alter the charge of intrinsically disordered proteins and thereby regulate their interactions. Here, the authors show that phosphorylation acts as an electrostatic rheostat for SRSF1- RNA binding, with binding free energy varying approximately linearly with net charge.

item.title: Nature Communications: PrimPol toggled by ATR modulates fork slowing and repriming under oncogenic KRAS-induced replication stress
item.description: Oncogenic KRAS causes replication stress that threatens genome stability during cancer development. Here, the authors show that ATR-regulated PrimPol switches between fork slowing and repriming modes to help cells tolerate KRAS-induced replication stress while limiting error-prone DNA synthesis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Repurposing the evolutionary fitness of marine bacteria for water-conserving conversion of lignin-derived carbon
item.description: Reverting waste carbon into chemicals with minimal freshwater use is essential for a sustainable future. Here, the authors engineer the marine bacterium R. nubinhibens , by decoupling bioproduction from central metabolism to convert lignin into chemicals with seawater as a water source.

item.title: Nature Communications: Amygdala beta bursts modulate hippocampal neuronal dynamics during human emotional processing
item.description: Neural mechanisms underlying emotional processing are not fully understood. Using intracranial recordings in humans, this study finds that transient amygdala beta bursts are associated with valence-dependent hippocampal neuronal activity, revealing temporally precise dynamics of emotional processing.

item.title: Nature Communications: A multiplexed wearable microfluidic platform for non-invasive sweat-inspired monitoring of plant guttation biomarkers
item.description: Plant sensors are emerging as key tools for precision agriculture, yet continuous monitoring of biomarkers in plant biofluids remains underdeveloped. Here, the authors introduce PlantIonics, a wearable microfluidic electrochemical platform for multiplexed, in situ analysis of guttation fluid. The system enables continuous, noninvasive monitoring of stress-associated plant physiological and metabolic responses under changing environmental conditions.

item.title: Nature Communications: Chromosome-scale assembly of yeast genomes using enzyme-free, dense optical genome mapping
item.description: Optical genome mapping (OGM) provides long-range genomic information but relies on sparse enzymatic labeling that restricts resolution in poorly labeled or structurally complex regions. Here the authors assemble yeast genomes at chromosome scale using dense OGM, resolving large repetitive regions.

item.title: Nature Communications: Parasitological efficacy of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine and amodiaquine for seasonal malaria chemoprevention in Africa
item.description: In this study, the authors show that post-treatment desethylamodiaquine concentration is the primary pharmacokinetic determinant of protection against malaria infection in African children who are given sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine and amodiaquine for seasonal malaria chemoprevention, with little apparent effect from sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine.
